clue.text: Candle 20 finds easy to carry around

parts.note: the cross-reference points to 20 across, whose answer in its 'dash' sense means rush
something easy to carry is light in weight

explanation.surface: Someone finds a candle handy to carry about.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 across is TEAR, read here as the verb 'to tear along', giving its synonym RUSH. A rushlight was a cheap candle made from a rush dipped in fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rushlight is a simple candle made of rush pith soaked in tallow.

clue.text: Prove wrong potato was picked up

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up reads the potato word from bottom to top

parts.note: a potato is a tuber

explanation.surface: A gardener disproves that the potato was harvested.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to refute, show an argument to be false.

clue.text: Run along quickly in small van

parts.note: a camper is a camper van

explanation.surface: Dashing off in a little camper.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to scurry, run along quickly.

clue.text: Hazel's dependants put woolly jumpers over formal dress

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the lambs on top of the other piece

parts.note: lambs are woolly and leap about
tails are a formal tailcoat

explanation.surface: Someone layers wool sweaters over evening wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly jumpers' are not sweaters but frisking lambs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambs' tails are the hanging catkins of the hazel tree.

clue.text: Imprisoned by king, I was a no-hoper

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held inside the king's letters

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Locked up by the monarch, I had no hope left.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone or something doomed, past saving.

clue.text: This colour ain't green, strangely enough

indicators.note: strangely signals that the letters of the words are in an odd order

explanation.surface: An orange-ish shade that is oddly not green.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerine is a deep orange colour named after the fruit.

clue.text: Henry's employed in pleasant and highly appropriate position

indicators.note: employed in means set to work inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: pleasant means nice
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry has landed an agreeable job that suits him perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or place exactly suited to someone.

clue.text: Informer is clued up, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to be clued up on something is to know it

explanation.surface: A police spy says he is well informed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nose is slang for a police informer.

clue.text: Letter expressing opposition to Italian wine

parts.note: chi is a Greek letter
anti means against

explanation.surface: A letter written in protest against an Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: Attention given to sheep set back by sheep-infesting parasite —- it's set aside

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: set back means turned round, so the sheep word reads backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a ked is a sheep tick

explanation.surface: A farmer watching sheep worried by ticks notes that one is reserved.
explanation.walkthrough: RAM reversed gives MAR. Earmarking was the marking of sheep's ears, so the scene fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked means reserved, allocated for a purpose.

clue.text: Caped crusader overcomes old bargee

indicators.note: in a across clue to overcome is to sit over and around, so the hero's name encloses the other piece

parts.note: the Caped Crusader is Batman, the comic-book hero

explanation.surface: A superhero defeats an elderly canal worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargee works a barge, as a boatman works a boat: near synonyms.

clue.text: Row following hospital's volte-face becomes more unpleasant

indicators.note: following places the row after the other piece
a volte-face is an about-turn, so the word for hospital is turned round

parts.note: a san, short for sanatorium, is a hospital
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: After the hospital reverses its policy, a quarrel turns nastier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as a quarrel but means a line of seats; 'volte-face' turns the hospital word round, and 'following' puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, meaning more unpleasant; 'becomes' is padding for the comparative.

clue.text: Records scores — they're put up on the wall

definitions.text: they're put up on the wall

parts.note: tapes are recordings
in rugby a try is a score

explanation.surface: A music fan's chart-topping hits are framed and hung up.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIES are scores in rugby football, worth five points each.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapestries are woven hangings hung on walls as decoration.

clue.text: Home care halved for ancient Indian

parts.note: at home means in

indicators.note: halved keeps the first half of the word care

explanation.surface: Domestic nursing cut in half for an old native.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the native people of ancient Peru, so an Indian of the Americas.

clue.text: Appeal in pamphlet received by people lacking a leader

indicators.note: received by means taken inside the other piece
lacking a leader drops the first letter of the people word

parts.note: a nation is a people
a tract is a pamphlet

explanation.surface: A leaflet's plea is taken up by a leaderless population.
explanation.walkthrough: NATION less its first letter is ATION, which takes TRACT in.
explanation.definitionFit: Attraction is appeal, the power to draw interest.

clue.text: Jacket father fastened round the chest

indicators.note: fastened round means wrapped about, so the father's letters enclose the chest

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
an ark is a chest, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Dad zipped a jacket up over his torso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' is the box, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket.

clue.text: Was perhaps performing neat steps

indicators.note: performing means putting on a show, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A dancer performing tidy steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was' is an example of the past tense, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Was is the past tense of the verb to be, an example of the category.

clue.text: Somewhat foolish and over the top

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both slightly stupid and, of behaviour, unreasonable or excessive.

clue.text: I hid spasm, shaken to the core on board

indicators.note: shaken means jumbled about, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: I hid a convulsion that shook me deeply while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaken to the core' looks like one phrase; 'to the core' belongs to the definition, the middle of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidships means in the middle part of a ship.

clue.text: Lackey has to pass on information in a specially prepared envelope

indicators.note: in places the passing-on and information inside the envelope

parts.note: an SAE is a stamped addressed envelope, prepared in advance for a reply
to tell is to pass on news
IT stands for information technology

explanation.surface: A minion must relay a message tucked inside a ready-stamped envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is a hanger-on or follower, figuratively orbiting someone powerful.

clue.text: Copy, with time flying

parts.note: flying means rushing, racing

explanation.surface: Duplicating something while time flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracing is a copy made through translucent paper.

clue.text: Made authoritative statement with several lines

definitions.meaning: issued a ruling, as a judge does

explanation.definitionFit: A judge ruled on a case; ruled paper is marked with straight lines.

clue.text: The French hit a snag — the dish is Italian

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

indicators.note: hit means struck and knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French cook runs into trouble making an Italian meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagna is a baked pasta dish from Italy.

clue.text: Drop wrench

explanation.definitionFit: A tear is a drop from the eye; to tear is to rip, wrench apart.

clue.text: Upset, is scared to get shunned

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Distressed and frightened of being cold-shouldered.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ostracised is to be excluded and avoided by a group.

clue.text: Survivor from the past about to enjoy ice-cream cone shortly?

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: you enjoy a cone by licking it

explanation.surface: An old-timer is about to tuck into an ice cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from an earlier time.

clue.text: Man about town welcomed by old and young

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in by the words, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: A socialite is greeted warmly by all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a fashionable man about town, a fop.

clue.text: Flower came up

explanation.definitionFit: A rose is a well-known bloom; rose is also the past tense of rise.

clue.text: Capital of Spain suffering setback after English became old

indicators.note: became means one letter turns into another
a setback is read as a going back, so the word for Spanish is turned round

parts.note: Iberian means of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A Spanish city in decline after the English grew old.
explanation.walkthrough: IBERIAN reversed is NAIREBI; its E becomes O.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Telling tales during confinement

parts.note: telling tales means telling lies
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: Gossiping while locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying-in is the old term for childbirth confinement.

clue.text: Standard or good score

definitions.meaning: a flag or emblem, like the Roman legion's ...
in golf, two under par on a hole

explanation.definitionFit: Roman legions carried an eagle as their standard; in golf it is two strokes under par.

clue.text: With time, a railway becomes less important

parts.note: a second is a unit of time

explanation.surface: Over time a railway line is downgraded.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondary means of lesser rank or importance.
